title: Renewal Runway: Compact QBR Decks and Playbook for Standard & Enterprise
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, repeatable QBR deck + ops playbook designed to be easy for CSMs to reuse across both Standard and Enterprise accounts. Goal: reduce prep time, improve consistency, and increase predictable renewal outcomes by aligning exec-level narrative with an operational follow-up tracker.

Intended audience:
- CSMs running recurring QBRs
- Renewal/Customer Success Managers planning playbooks
- Solutions Engineers who join for tech updates

Notes to self (style guidance):
- Keep decks under 12 slides for standard accounts, up to 18 for enterprise (include appendix).
- Use one slide to tell the 3-line renewal story (health, adoption, ask).
- Use tokenized metrics (API calls, avg latency, cost delta) for product-savvy customers; use business outcomes for execs.

1) Template: Standard QBR (compact, 10 slides) — Purpose: high-touch renewal conversation for < $50k ARR accounts
- Cover / Agenda (1 slide): objective, time, attendees, ask
- Where we started (1 slide): key metrics baseline (adoption, uptime, latency, cost per request)
- What changed (2 slides): top 3 wins, top 2 risks (inc. incidents), customer quotes/feedback
- Usage & ROI snapshot (2 slides): usage trends, cost efficiency moves (batching / cache gains), initial ROI bullets
- Roadmap alignment (1 slide): near-term features relevant to customer; expected impact
- Success plan & commitments (1 slide): action items, owners, timelines
- Renewal ask + options (1 slide): timeline, discount/packaging options, recommended next steps
- Appendix / links (optional)

Speaker notes (standard):
- Open with a 30s recap of relationship and value realized.
- Focus on two priorities customer cares about.
- Close with a single next-step ask (e.g., commit to 1-year, pilot dedicated pool).

2) Template: Enterprise QBR (expanded, 14–18 slides) — Purpose: strategic renewal for > $50k ARR, multi-stakeholder
- Cover / Exec summary (1 slide): meeting objective, renewal horizon, primary decision-makers
- Topline health signal (1 slide): CSAT, adoption index, incident SLOs, usage at 90/95th pct
- Business impact stories (2 slides): short case studies/internal references of how product reduced latency/cost or increased throughput
- Technical deep-dive (2 slides): architecture diagram, upcoming features impacting scale/security (KV caching, quantization profile changes)
- Performance & cost analysis (2 slides): per-token cost trend, batching/caching impact, suggested optimization levers
- Risk register & mitigation (1 slide): open items, timeline, impact assessment
- Contract & renewal options (2 slides): recommended term, tiering, SLA adjustments, migration path to Dedicated/Private if requested
- Rollout & change management (1 slide): steps for infra/ops teams, required approvals, support model
- Success metrics & eval plan (1 slide): specific metrics to gate renewal, sample prompts/test sets for quality checks
- Action plan / owners (1 slide): 30/60/90 day commitments, named owners from both sides
- Appendix (2–3 slides): logs/observability samples, security attestations, legal notes

Playbook: Pre-QBR (checklist)
- 28 days out: confirm renewal horizon and attendees, surface contract terms, request usage and billing export (last 6 months).
- 14 days out: send pre-read with 3 priority questions for customer to answer; schedule SE dry-run if enterprise.
- 7 days out: internal alignment sync (AE + CSM + SE): finalize slides, confirm ask and any concessions.
- 3 days out: populate tracker row with proposed offers and approval matrix, share deck link with customer with request to review.

Playbook: During QBR (runbook)
- 0-5 min: quick intro and expected outcomes
- 5-20 min: product/usage highlights (CSM leads)
- 20-35 min: business impact and roadmap alignment (AE/Customer exec)
- 35-50 min: technical deep dive / risks (SE leads)
- Final 10 min: clear ask and next steps; confirm owner for each action in tracker

Playbook: Post-QBR (follow-up and renewal orchestration)
- Within 24h: share final slide deck + action tracker; send calendar invites for next checkpoints
- Within 3 business days: convert approved offer to a draft order form and route through approvals (AE + revenue ops)
- Weekly cadence: update tracker with progress; escalate blockers at week 2 if procurement/finance hold up

Renewal Tracker (compact row format — recommended columns)
- account_id, account_owner, renewal_date, ARR, recommended_term, recommended_price, current_commitment, risk_score (0-10), last_meeting_notes, next_action_owner, next_action_due

Example tracker row (text sample):
- acct: Skylark AI, owner: Jordan Patel, renewal: 2025-02-28, ARR: $72,000, rec_term: 12m, rec_price: $65,000, current: $60,000, risk: 3, notes: "adoption up 45% q/q; legal wants 3rd-party security attestation", next_owner: Marisol Vega, due: 2025-01-20

Conversation starters / scripts (CSM quick lines)
- Exec: "Over the last 6 months you reduced inference spend by ~22% after we enabled adaptive batching — does that align with the savings you expected?"
- Engineering: "We saw tail latency drop 35% on your worst-case queries after the KV cache change — want to review a short runbook so your team can replicate?"
- Procurement: "If we move to a 12-month committed tier we can lock current pricing; would you like us to prepare a draft PO for review?"

Risk scoring rubric (suggested)
- 0-3: Low — strong adoption, no open credits, stakeholder engaged
- 4-6: Medium — usage flat or small declines, 1–2 open action items
- 7-10: High — churn signals: execs unreachable, feature regressions, unresolved security requests

Metrics pack (what to include in pre-read / appendix)
- Usage: API calls by endpoint, tokens per request distribution, peak qps, daily active integrations
- Reliability: 7/30/90 day error rates, incident timelines, SLO attainment
- Cost: per-token cost, batching/caching savings, suggested quantization option and estimated savings
- Quality: eval results on agreed prompt set (pass/fail and short examples)

Concessions playbook (decision matrix)
- For Low risk: standard renewal, limited discount (0–5%), add-on credits for training or onboarding
- For Medium risk: structured pilot for Dedicated or Enablement package, 5–10% discount conditional on multi-year commitment
- For High risk: escalate to renewals lead, consider short-term bridge contracts and formal remediation plan

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Confirm which legal artifacts are required for enterprise renewals in EMEA (Marisol to confirm).
- Draft short email templates for pre-read and thank-you follow-ups (include sample subject lines).
- Decide if we standardize to a single risk scale across CS and RevOps (proposal: keep 0-10 but normalize weightings).

Appendix: sample slide titles (copy/paste friendly)
- "Executive summary: outcome and renewal ask"
- "Customer health: adoption & reliability snapshot"
- "Top impact examples: business stories"
- "Technical review: ops & infra highlights"
- "Renewal options & recommended path"
- "Action plan & owners (30/60/90)"

Quick templates (email snippets)
- Pre-read request subject: "QBR pre-read: 30m on [date] — 3 quick questions"
- Thank you + next steps subject: "Thanks — QBR summary + next steps"
- Sample ask line: "Based on what we discussed, our recommendation is a 12-month renewal at [tier] to secure pricing and support — shall I route a draft order now?"

Linked resources / references (internal):
- CS playbook master (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-1234-qbr-guidelines
- Renewal approval flow (Jira): JIRA-CS-987
- Template slide pack (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/qbr-templates/pull/45

Document history / edits:
- 2024-10-18: initial outline (Avery)
- 2024-11-02: added enterprise deep-dive & risk rubric (Jordan)
- 2024-12-15: added tracker row example + concessions matrix (Marisol)
- 2025-01-12: cleaned speaker notes and email snippets; set to draft ready for peer review (Avery)

Notes to future self: keep the deck modular — cut the appendix for standard accounts, expand for enterprise with technical artifacts. Aim to reduce average prep time to < 2 hours per QBR by pre-populating tracker rows and reusing past decks where possible.
